title: Request Lifecycle
markdown:
A single chat message makes a full round-trip through the API, the orchestrator's tool-use loop, a parallel specialist fan-out, and synthesis — all streamed back as server-sent events.

### Steps

1. **Arrival** — the client posts to `POST /chat` (`openexecutive.api.routes.chat`). The turn carries a `<current_speaker>` hint resolved from the caller's `person_id`, plus a `<briefing>` digest of current open alerts (built in parallel with RAG/episodic/peer-memory fetches) so the Executive can discuss any item shown on the `/today` briefing page A turn arriving from a chat adapter instead of the web app also carries a `<channel>` block naming the surface and stating which approvals can be completed there; on Slack the `<briefing>` digest is gated to the principal's DMs. All three ride in the **user turn**, never a cached system block.
2. **Tool-use loop** — the `Executive` calls Claude. For a cross-domain question the assistant turn emits multiple `consult_specialist` tool-use blocks at once.
3. **Parallel fan-out** — `openexecutive.orchestrator.router.route_parallel` dispatches those calls concurrently, bounded by `MAX_PARALLEL_SPECIALISTS`; calls past the cap get a skip tool_result.
4. **Per-specialist RAG** — each specialist runs its own domain-filtered ChromaDB query, then reasons over the retrieved chunks and returns analysis as a tool_result.
5. **Synthesis** — the Executive feeds the tool_results back to Claude and streams one coherent reply; a `thinking` keepalive covers the specialist round.
6. **Optional committee review** — when enabled, `Executive.stream_chat_with_committee()` runs a silent draft, parallel reviewer critiques, then a streamed revision pass.
7. **Side effects** — any side-effecting tool call surfaces an `action_taken` chip; the stream closes with a `done` event. One side-effecting tool is gated server-side rather than by its description: `ack_alert` will only accept an `alert_id` from the live alert board the server itself derived this turn — the whole live set, not only the rows the `<briefing>` digest printed, since `/today` renders more cards than the digest lists and every one of them is Discuss-able — and it fails closed, so an id it cannot even parse is refused rather than waved through to the handler's own parse. That check runs on **every** session. It used to run only on turns that arrived from a chat channel, keyed on `origin_channel`, which the browser never sets — so the web, the surface the principal actually uses, was unchecked and the model could ack any id, including one quoted out of an alert body by the briefing page's Discuss handoff. What that buys is bounded and worth stating plainly: an id that is invented, closed, snoozed or expired is refused, including one quoted out of an attacker-written alert body; the model being argued into acking the wrong *live* card is not prevented. A session that was shown no board has an empty trusted set and can ack nothing, so the unattended passes (the nightly reflection, the research synthesis) are now refused by default — they also still withhold the tool outright, which is belt-and-braces rather than the only thing stopping them.
8. **Tool failures** — a handler that raises instead of returning its JSON error is isolated: both tool gathers run with `return_exceptions=True`, the model gets an error `tool_result` naming only the exception's TYPE — a message can carry a filesystem path, a validation error echoing the input, or a third-party HTTP body, and anything in model context can be quoted back to the user, so the full repr stays in the log and the audit row — and the failure is audited with `ok=false`. Only `CancelledError` is re-raised, so turn-timeout and client-disconnect handling still work. Before this one crashing tool aborted the whole turn, which reached the user as an unexplained apology with no audit row (#136).

Web search, when invoked on the Anthropic path, executes inside the Anthropic API itself (`web_search_20250305`) and returns within the same generation; for any model routed via OpenRouter the same tool becomes OpenRouter's `openrouter:web_search` server tool, which also runs inside the generation with the same search cap and domain lists.

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant API as FastAPI /chat
  participant E as Executive
  participant CL as Claude
  participant S as Specialists
  participant KB as ChromaDB
  C->>API: POST /chat message
  API->>E: start turn
  E->>CL: messages (tool-use loop)
  CL-->>E: consult_specialist calls
  E->>S: route_parallel fan-out
  S->>KB: domain-filtered RAG
  KB-->>S: chunks
  S-->>E: analysis tool_results
  E->>CL: synthesize
  CL-->>E: streamed reply
  E-->>API: SSE chunks then done
  API-->>C: streamed response
